meta.title: Computable

home.title: Computable
home.lead: Computable is a place to learn the Turing machine by running one, step by step.
home.caption: This is Turing's first machine, from his 1936 paper. It prints 0 1 0 1 … on every other cell and never stops.

step.ready: Ready. The head starts on cell {cell} in state {state}.
step.write: In {state} reading {symbol}: write {write}, {move, select, L {move left} R {move right} other {stay}}, go to {next}.
step.noRule: In {state} reading {symbol}: no rule matches, so the machine stops.
step.back: Stepped back. State {state}, head on cell {cell}.

result.accepted: Accepted after {steps, plural, one {# step} other {# steps}}. The tape now reads {tape}.
result.acceptedBlank: Accepted after {steps, plural, one {# step} other {# steps}}. The tape is now blank.
result.rejectState: Rejected: the machine reached {state} after {steps, plural, one {# step} other {# steps}}.

result.limit: Paused after {limit, number} steps. This machine may never halt. Continue?

issue.badBlank: The blank must be exactly one symbol.
issue.acceptAndReject: {state} is both an accept state and a reject state. A state can only be one.
issue.emptyState: Rule {rule}: {field, select, state {the state} other {the next state}} is empty.
issue.badSymbol: Rule {rule}: {field, select, read {the symbol it reads} other {the symbol it writes}} must be exactly one symbol.
issue.badOp: Rule {rule}: “{op}” is not an operation. Use P and a symbol, E, L or R.
issue.duplicateRule: Rules {first} and {rule}: two rules for {state} reading {symbol}. A Turing machine needs exactly one.

warning.stateWithoutRules: {state} has no rules yet. The machine will stop there and reject.
warning.legacyDuplicateRow: Lines {row} and {keptRow} both give a rule for {state} reading {symbol}. The machine uses line {keptRow}, as the 2016 app did.

table.title: Rules
table.hint: Each row is one rule. The machine finds the row for its state and the symbol under the head. Type in a cell to change a rule.

fieldHint.badOp: Use P and a symbol, E, L or R.

table.duplicate: Two rules for {state} reading {symbol}. A Turing machine needs exactly one.

settings.acceptAndReject: A state cannot both accept and reject.
settings.leftEdgeReject: On this tape, a move left of cell 0 rejects, as in the 2016 app.

diagram.title: State diagram
diagram.hint: The same rules drawn as arrows. Circles are states. A double circle accepts, a dashed circle rejects, and the arrow on the left points at the start state. The rule table lists the same rules as text.

about.title: About Computable
about.lead: Computable began in 2016 as a capstone project for a degree in Computer Science at UNASP: a Turing machine simulator for the web.
about.rebuilt: In 2026 the author rebuilt it from scratch as Computable. The simulator still opens the machines saved by the 2016 app.
about.project: Simulador de Máquina de Turing, Uma Aplicação Web para o Ensino
about.projectEnglish: (A Turing machine simulator: a web app for teaching)
about.author: Wellmmer Lucas de Oliveira Pinto
about.tag: See the 2016 app's code at the git tag v1.0-tcc-2016

privacy.title: Privacy
privacy.lead: Computable has no accounts, sets no cookies and keeps no personal data about you.
privacy.browser: Your browser keeps your current machine and your choice of squared or night paper. They stay on your device. Computable never sends them anywhere.
privacy.shareLink: A share link holds the machine after the # sign. Browsers do not send that part of a link to any server.

analytics.title: What the site counts
analytics.summary: To learn which pages help people, the site counts visits with {service}. It sets no cookies.
analytics.counted: For each page view it records the time, the page, the page you came from, your country, region and city, your browser, your system and the kind of device.
analytics.visitor: It tells visits apart with a code made from the request, and throws the code away after 24 hours. It does not tie the visits to you or to your IP address.

privacy.donations: The Support page only links to payment services, such as PayPal and Ko-fi. You pay on their pages, under their privacy rules. No payment data passes through Computable.

support.title: Buy the dev a coffee
support.lead: Computable is free, with no ads and no accounts. If it helped you learn, a coffee helps me keep building it.
